exercise.name: Lever Bicep Curl

reference.title: Lever Bicep Curl
reference.listing: Animated GIF (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Seated arm curl machine (sloped arm pad, lever with handles aligned with the elbows)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.3 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Stack load is user-chosen: curl without lifting the elbows off the pad.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate; slower lowering

cues.text: Sit with the chest against the pad edge and the backs of the upper arms on the sloped pad, elbows lined up with the lever axis; palms up on the handle, arms nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the handle up toward the shoulders, elbows staying on the pad.
Squeeze the biceps at the top without letting the elbows lift.
Breathe in and lower under control along the arc.
Stop with the arms nearly straight, keeping tension on the biceps.

mistakes.fix: Keep the backs of the arms on the pad; lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows not lined up with the lever axis
mistakes.fix: Set the seat so the elbows sit on the pivot line.

kinematics.peak: ≈124° at the top of the curl
kinematics.norm: From nearly straight to fully bent, the forearm stopping short of vertical (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: On the pad, sloping 40° down and forward
kinematics.peak: Elbow within 0.1 cm of the pivot
kinematics.norm: Upper arm resting on the sloped pad; the elbow stays on the lever axis (clinical opinion)
Supinated: palms up on the handle (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Pivot 81.4 cm high, 18.5 cm ahead of the shoulders
kinematics.peak: Lever swings 109.8°; hands within 0.09 cm of the arc
kinematics.norm: The handle rides an arc about the elbow: the lever pivot is lined up with the elbow joint (clinical opinion)
Machine and cable curls rank among the higher-activation biceps exercises; arm position on the pad changes biceps length (ACE 2014; Oliveira 2009)

kinematics.setup: Pause 0.5 s with the arms long
kinematics.peak: 1.3 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down
kinematics.norm: About 1.3 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #2072, Lever Bicep Curl, animated GIF (movement reference)
Young, Porcari, Camic, Kovacs and Foster 2014, ACE-sponsored EMG study of eight biceps exercises, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse (ACE ProSource, August 2014)
Oliveira, Matta, Alves, Garcia and Vieira 2009, effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls (J Sports Sci Med 8(1):24-29)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Stack load is user-chosen: start light; keep the elbows on the pad.
Do not let the handle drop into the straight-arm position.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Elbow discomfort at the bottom: stop just short of straight arms.
progressions: Pause for 2 s at the top.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Prime mover: bends the elbow and turns the palm up.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Prime mover: bends the elbow and turns the palm up.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the handles and help bend the elbow (brachioradialis).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the handles and help bend the elbow (brachioradialis).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm on the pad.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arm on the pad.
